title: Arnoraja and the Lake of Ana Sagar

title_i18n.en: Arnoraja and the Lake of Ana Sagar

subtitle: On a Battlefield of Sand, a King Raises a Sea of Stone and Water
era: Hydraulic engineering at Ajmer, c. 1135-1150 CE
region: Ajmer and the Bandi river valley, Rajasthan
moral: The measure of a ruler is whether he leaves a battlefield as a graveyard or as a reservoir.

sources.note: Directly attributes the lake to Arnoraja, built on the battle-plain.

sources.citation: Chahamana prashasti cited in R. B. Singh, History of the Chahamanas (1964)
sources.note: Records the Pushkar-area victory and the lake-building.

sources.citation: Dasharatha Sharma, Early Chauhan Dynasties (1959), pp. 43-46
sources.note: Reign chronology and the Ana Sagar project.

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Arnoraja on a rocky embankment above a vast shimmering lake, faint outlines of old battlements and hills of Ajmer behind

dialogue.text: On the field where he once broke a Ghaznavid raid, King Arnoraja dammed a restless river and left Ajmer a lake that still shines today.

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye over the arid plains near Ajmer, distant dust clouds of cavalry approaching a cluster of temples and groves at Pushkar

dialogue.text: In the mid-twelfth century, a Ghaznavid force rode deep into Rajputana, their dust reaching the sacred ponds and shrines near Pushkar.

panels.shot: dramatic mid-shot of Arnoraja armoured on horseback, standard of the Chahamanas behind, pointing his sword toward the distant enemy

dialogue.text: King Arnoraja of the Chahamanas, grandson of Ajmer’s founders, rode out to meet them on the open plain beyond Ajmer.

panels.shot: wide battlefield tableau showing opposing cavalry lines poised, shields glinting, a faint depression in the land hinting at an old watercourse

dialogue.text: The chronicler Jayanaka remembers a hard-fought field, near a shallow valley of the Bandi river, where spears met and a Ghaznavid raid was turned back.

panels.shot: low-angle close-up on Arnoraja post-battle, standing amid trampled earth and discarded arms, gazing toward the shallow river course

dialogue.text: Legend loves the clash of arms; the Prithviraja-Vijaya pauses instead on what Arnoraja saw after the din faded—the thin, wandering Bandi cutting across the scarred plain.

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Arnoraja looking over the valley, with farmers in the far distance leading bullocks along dry fields

dialogue.text: Ajmer’s hills held forts and shrines, but its people watched the sky each year. Rains were short, wells were few, and the Bandi flowed away, untamed.

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Arnoraja’s thoughtful face, a faint overlay of water ripples reflected in his eyes

dialogue.speaker: arnoraja
dialogue.text: This field has drunk war. Let it drink rain instead.

panels.shot: wide shot of a royal council in an open pavilion, Arnoraja seated on a low throne with engineers and ministers unrolling palm-leaf plans

dialogue.text: Jayanaka records the king’s decision: on that very battlefield, Arnoraja would raise an embankment, spread the Bandi’s waters, and bind Ajmer’s fate to a lake of his own making.

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of early construction, workers and elephants moving stone blocks across the valley floor, a line of surveyors with simple sighting tools

dialogue.text: Great earthworks demand more than will. Surveyors traced gradients, builders cut and placed stone, and the king’s treasury turned from horses and wars to a wall of earth and rock.

panels.shot: low, ground-level shot along the rising bund, men packing earth, ramming it with wooden pounders, the unfinished crest stretching toward the horizon

dialogue.text: Block by block, tamped layer upon layer, the Ana Sagar bund rose. The Chahamana prashasti remembers this labour as clearly as any campaign.

panels.shot: evocative mid-shot of Arnoraja personally inspecting a stone spillway, pointing while a mason chisels, clouds building in the monsoon sky

dialogue.text: This was no simple pond. Channels, spillways and sluices controlled the Bandi’s moods, so that floods would not tear the new heart of Ajmer apart.

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of the first monsoon filling the basin, rain slanting down, villagers watching from the slopes as water spreads

dialogue.text: Then the rains came. The basin filled, the old field disappeared, and where horses once charged, the waters of Ana Sagar spread in a gleaming expanse.

panels.shot: tranquil sunrise wide shot of the completed lake, fishermen in small boats, women drawing water, Ajmer’s walls and temples above

dialogue.text: Around its shores, life changed. Fields found new irrigation, cattle new watering, and Ajmer’s markets and houses turned toward the lake that bore their king’s name.

panels.shot: mid-shot inside a temple courtyard, Arnoraja overseeing sculptors working on a Shiva image, with an inscription stone being carved nearby

dialogue.text: The same reign that dammed the Bandi also raised a shrine for his father, Naradeva, in Ajmer. Stone, water and inscription tied lineage, faith and engineering together.

panels.shot: ornate court scene mid-shot, Arnoraja seated beside a queen in Gujarati attire, with a Chaulukya envoy presenting gifts

dialogue.text: Through marriage he linked Ajmer to Gujarat: Kanchanadevi, daughter of Jayasimha Siddharaja, sat beside him. Alliances, like embankments, held only as long as pressures were balanced.

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Arnoraja older, looking out over Ana Sagar from a palace balcony, distant hills hazy

dialogue.text: By the time new wars flared with Kumarapala of Gujarat, Ana Sagar’s waters had already outlasted the first treaties, a quieter monument than any victory pillar.

panels.shot: tight, tense interior shot in a dim palace corridor, Jagaddeva’s silhouette behind Arnoraja, who is unaware, shadows heavy

dialogue.text: Yet the threat that ended Arnoraja’s life did not ride from Ghazni or Gujarat. Chroniclers state it came from within his own house.

panels.shot: stark close-up of Arnoraja falling or collapsing out of frame, his crown tumbling, no violence shown, only shock on his face

dialogue.text: The sources speak bluntly: Jagaddeva killed his own father. A king who had broken invaders and dammed a river was cut down by his son’s hand.

panels.shot: time-lapse-style wide shot: Ana Sagar across centuries, old palaces, later pavilions, modern city edges and cranes faintly suggested along the shores

dialogue.text: Today Ana Sagar still holds Ajmer’s sky, even as courts debate encroachments and pollution. Arnoraja’s name endures here not in legend alone, but in stone and water that outlived his own bloodline.
